PLAN "12-Week Postpartum Return Programme: Summary"
TYPE workout
VISIBILITY public

GOALS
  GOAL primary strength:
    name "gentle postpartum recovery and progressive strength"
  GOAL secondary cardio:
    name "improve cardiovascular fitness safely postpartum"
  GOAL secondary nutrition:
    name "support breastfeeding and postpartum recovery"

PHASES
  PHASE "Phase 1: Early Recovery" (2 weeks):
    summary:
      - "Focus: Gentle mobility, walking, and light stretching."
      - "Strength: Cat_cow, bird_dog, child_pose, hip_flexor_stretch, hamstring_stretch."
      - "Cardio: Short, easy walks (15–20 min, 1–2x/week)."
      - "No direct core or high-intensity work."
      - "Frequency: 2 mobility/strength sessions + 1 walk per week."
      - "Intensity: RPE 2–3."
  PHASE "Phase 2: Gentle Strength, Mobility & Cardio" (4 weeks):
    summary:
      - "Focus: Continue mobility, introduce gentle strength (glute_bridge), increase walking duration."
      - "Strength: Cat_cow, bird_dog, glute_bridge, step_up (added late), hip_flexor_stretch, hamstring_stretch."
      - "Cardio: Walks increase to 22–27 min, 1x/week."
      - "No direct core or high-intensity work unless cleared at 6 weeks."
      - "Frequency: 2 strength/mobility + 1 walk per week."
      - "Intensity: RPE 3–4."
  PHASE "Phase 3: Progressive Strength, Cardio & Mobility" (6 weeks):
    summary:
      - "Focus: Progressive strength (higher sets/reps, add squat, lunge), more challenging walking/cardio."
      - "Strength: Cat_cow, bird_dog, glute_bridge, step_up, squat, lunge, hip_flexor_stretch, hamstring_stretch."
      - "Cardio: Walks up to 42 min, 2x/week (Wed/Sat), RPE 5–6."
      - "Intensity: Strength work increases to RPE 6–9 by week 12."
      - "Frequency: 2 strength/mobility + 2 cardio walks per week."
      - "If cleared at 6+ weeks, gentle core activation (bird_dog, cat_cow, glute_bridge) may be continued; avoid crunch, plank, sit_up, leg_raise until diastasis recti is screened and healed."
      - "No HIIT or impact work before week 12 and only with medical clearance."

NUTRITION
  NUTRITION_PLAN "Breastfeeding Support":
    description "A nutrition plan to support breastfeeding, postpartum recovery, and energy needs."
    guidelines:
      - "Increase daily caloric intake by 400–500 kcal for milk production."
      - "Prioritize hydration: 2.5–3 liters water/day."
      - "Protein at every meal, complex carbs, healthy fats, 5+ servings fruits/vegetables."
      - "Continue prenatal/postnatal multivitamin as recommended."
      - "Limit caffeine, avoid alcohol, minimize processed foods."
      - "Eat frequent, small meals/snacks for energy."
      - "Monitor baby's response to foods; consult healthcare provider as needed."
    sample_day:
      breakfast: "Oatmeal with berries, chia seeds, and a glass of milk."
      snack_1: "Greek yogurt with sliced banana and walnuts."
      lunch: "Grilled chicken breast, quinoa, steamed broccoli, and olive oil drizzle."
      snack_2: "Whole grain toast with avocado and tomato."
      dinner: "Baked salmon, sweet potato, and mixed green salad."
      snack_3: "Carrot sticks and hummus, or cottage cheese with fruit."
    hydration:
      - "Start the day with a large glass of water."
      - "Drink a glass of water at every meal and snack."
      - "Keep a water bottle nearby during breastfeeding sessions."
    notes:
      - "Adjust portion sizes based on hunger, energy, and weight changes."
      - "Consult a registered dietitian for personalized nutrition support if needed."

NOTES
  - "Direct core/abs work (crunch, plank, sit_up, leg_raise, etc.) should NOT be introduced until at least 6 weeks post-C-section and only after OB or pelvic floor PT clearance."
  - "HIIT or high-impact cardio should NOT be introduced until at least 12 weeks postpartum and only after medical clearance, with a gradual, low-impact start."
  - "Progress intensity in strength and cardio in phase 3 to help her feel strong by week 12."
  - "Monitor for any symptoms (pain, bulging, incontinence, heaviness) and regress if needed."
  - "Always prioritize pelvic floor engagement and breathing with all core and strength work."
  - "Consult a pelvic floor specialist or postpartum exercise professional for individualized progression."
